source.title: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
source.authors: Junnan Li; Dongxu Li; S. Savarese; S. Hoi

record.tranche_reason: The study reports downstream VQA results for differently sized language models in a vision-language setting, but does not test language-model pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The study reports model-size comparisons on downstream VQA, which bear on V6. It does not report held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy, power-law fits, large-run predictions, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Table 2's extracted layout does not support reliable assignment of its individual scores, so only the authors' explicit qualitative size comparison is recorded from it.
record.test_reason: BLIP-2 is a vision-language method paper. It compares two or three sizes of a frozen LLM plugged into its system, with no loss measurements, no power-law fit and no prediction across scale. That incidental size comparison does not bear on whether any version holds, including V6's 'predictably'. It cites Hoffmann et al. only to explain an OK-VQA gap.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say a stronger image encoder or stronger LLM gives better zero-shot VQA: ViT-g beats ViT-L, larger same-family LLMs beat smaller ones, and FlanT5 beats OPT. They frame this as BLIP-2 being able to harvest unimodal advances. They draw no scaling-law conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: This is a vision-language pretraining study that compares downstream task scores across selected model sizes; it does not reproduce the original language-model loss-scaling measurements or fitting procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: Swapping in a larger frozen LLM from the same family mostly raises zero-shot VQA scores (Table 2). VQAv2 val: OPT2.7B 53.5 vs OPT6.7B 54.3. OK-VQA: 31.7 vs 36.4. FlanT5XL 63.1 vs FlanT5XXL 65.2. Fine-tuned VQAv2 gains are small (81.59 vs 82.19). On COCO captioning the larger OPT is slightly worse (CIDEr 145.8 vs 145.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In modular VLMs with a frozen LLM, larger frozen LLMs within a family give modestly better downstream vision-language scores, not uniformly across tasks.

record.problems: No power-law fit or prediction test is reported. The VQA size comparisons cover selected models and do not establish a predictive scaling relationship; the study reports no uncertainty estimates for these scores.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 individual score assignments were left out because the supplied flattened text does not reliably map all values to model and metric columns; its qualitative same-family size result is recorded in r3.

untested.parts: No pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
No shape ablations at fixed size.
No power-law fits for vision-language training.
No fitted or predictive relationship between downstream score and scale or loss; only 2–3 sizes of a frozen LLM.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports' label is dropped. The comparisons concern a frozen sub-component and cover at most two sizes per family, without any predictive fit. Captioning results (Table 3) are mixed across sizes. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute; power-law form and range.
Predictions of larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation as a function of compute.
Effects of language-model depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss results in other modalities or training regimes; the study does not measure such losses or fit power laws.
The study reports selected VQA comparisons, but does not fit a predictive relationship between downstream performance and scale or pretraining loss, or test other downstream tasks for this purpose.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.
